findings.title: acceptEdits auto-allows FileWrite of language REPL/debugger cwd init files (.pdbrc, .Rprofile, .irbrc, .ghci, …) that parallel blocked shell rcs.
findings.description: DISTINCT from filed shell-rc blocks (.bashrc/.zshrc/.profile), Gemfile/setup.py install eval, vite/jest/eslint JS configs, and Makefile/justfile/Taskfile build recipes. Under acceptEdits, in-cwd writes auto-allow after checkPathSafetyForAutoEdit. DANGEROUS_FILES intentionally lists shell startup basenames (.bashrc, .bash_profile, .zshrc, .zprofile, .profile) plus .gitconfig/.mcp.json/.ripgreprc/.claude.json, but omits language REPL and debugger cwd init files that auto-execute on a normal later session start: .pdbrc (Python pdb), .Rprofile/.Renviron (R), .irbrc/.pryrc (Ruby IRB/Pry), .ghci (GHCi), .ocamlinit (OCaml toplevel), and .gdbinit/.lldbinit (debuggers; gdb may also gate on auto-load safe-path). DANGEROUS_DIRECTORIES is only .git/.vscode/.idea/.claude. FileWrite/FileEdit of those init files therefore auto-allows. Live bun checkPathSafetyForAutoEdit: all listed inits AUTO; .bashrc/.mcp.json ASK. Live PoC: planted .pdbrc ran under python3 -m pdb and wrote a marker; CPython pdb.Pdb.__init__ documents Read ~/.pdbrc and ./.pdbrc and opens ".pdbrc". Project settings can set permissions.defaultMode acceptEdits with no BypassPermissionsModeDialog.
findings.impact: After generic Trust plus acceptEdits (project-planted or user-selected), the model can silently plant REPL/debugger startup code. The next python -m pdb, R, irb/pry, ghci, ocaml, or gdb/lldb session in the repo executes attacker code as the victim — delayed RCE without a Write prompt, via the same threat class DANGEROUS_FILES already tried to cover for shell rcs.
findings.attack_path:
1. Attacker commits CLAUDE.md instructing a 'debug/REPL helper' write of .pdbrc / .Rprofile / .irbrc / .ghci / .ocamlinit / .gdbinit (optional: .claude/settings.json permissions.defaultMode acceptEdits).
2. Victim clones, reviews the tree (no malicious init yet), and trusts the folder. TrustDialog is generic; acceptEdits does not show Bypass Permissions.
3. FileWrite of the init file passes isDangerousFilePathToAutoEdit (basename absent from DANGEROUS_FILES; no parent in DANGEROUS_DIRECTORIES) and is auto-allowed because the path is inside cwd.
4. Victim later runs a normal toolchain command in that directory (python -m pdb, R, irb, ghci, ocaml, gdb/lldb). The tool auto-sources the planted cwd init and executes attacker code.
findings.remediation: Add .pdbrc, .Rprofile, .Renviron, .irbrc, .pryrc, .ghci, .ocamlinit, .gdbinit, .lldbinit (and similar language REPL/debugger cwd inits) to DANGEROUS_FILES alongside the existing shell rc list. Do not honor defaultMode acceptEdits from projectSettings without disclosing it. Require an explicit prompt for writes that become auto-sourced session startup code.
findings.why_distinct: Not shell rcs (those are already blocked). Not Gemfile/setup.py/JS-config/Makefile (install/build eval). Trigger is REPL/debugger session start auto-sourcing cwd inits — the missing parallel to .bashrc in DANGEROUS_FILES.
findings.poc_video_notes: Live PoC: python3 -m pdb with planted ./.pdbrc executed os.system and created a marker file. bun checkPathSafetyForAutoEdit returned AUTO for .pdbrc/.Rprofile/.irbrc/.pryrc/.ghci/.ocamlinit/.gdbinit/.lldbinit and ASK for .bashrc/.mcp.json. R/irb/ghci/ocaml/gdb were not installed on this host; those siblings rely on documented cwd auto-load. A live acceptEdits FileWrite REPL session was not run. Marker contents omitted.
